Safety Systems
ISO 13849 Performance Level: PLr Risk Graph, PFHd Bands, Categories, MTTFd, DC, CCF and a Guard Door Solved Example

Machine safety circuits are rated with a letter from PL a to PL e, and that letter decides how good your interlocks, relays and contactors must be. This guide walks through the risk graph, the PFHd table, MTTFd, DC and CCF with a worked guard door example.

PLr Risk Graph PFHd Table Categories B to 4 MTTFd from B10d SISTEMA

Performance Level tells you how reliably a machine safety function does its job. Here we decode every parameter behind it and calculate a real guard door interlock step by step.

Hello everyone, today we are going to understand the iso 13849 performance level, how PLr is chosen and how PL a to PL e is proven with numbers.

What Is ISO 13849 Performance Level?

The ISO 13849 performance level (PL) is a five step rating, from PL a to PL e, that states how reliably a safety related part of a machine control system performs its safety function. It is expressed as the average probability of a dangerous failure per hour, called PFHd, where PL e is the most reliable band.

Quick Answer
  • PL a to PL e is set by PFHd, the average probability of dangerous failure per hour.
  • PL e means PFHd from 10minus 8 up to below 10minus 7 per hour.
  • The required level PLr comes from a risk graph using severity S, frequency F and avoidance P.
  • Achieved PL depends on Category, MTTFd, DCavg and CCF (65 points or more).
  • MTTFd of electromechanical parts = B10d ÷ (0.1 × nop).

ISO 13849 Part 1 covers the design of safety related parts of control systems on machines, from a door switch to a full safety PLC. Each safety function, such as stopping a motor when a guard opens, gets its own ISO 13849 performance level, while Part 2 covers validation.

Do You Know?

The 2006 edition of ISO 13849 Part 1 replaced the old EN 954 approach, which only looked at circuit structure, and added MTTFd, DCavg and CCF so that reliability numbers finally became part of the rating.

Advertisement

How Is PLr Determined From the Risk Graph?

PLr is the required performance level that comes out of your risk assessment, before any circuit is drawn. ISO 13849 Part 1 gives a simple risk graph with three yes or no style questions, and many engineers sketch it next to the risk matrix used in hazard studies.

1
Severity S
S1 is slight, normally reversible injury. S2 is serious, normally irreversible injury or death.
2
Frequency F
F1 is seldom to less often and or brief exposure. F2 is frequent to continuous and or long exposure.
3
Avoidance P
P1 means avoiding the hazard is possible under specific conditions. P2 means it is scarcely possible.
4
Read PLr
Follow the branches to the end of the graph to read PLr from a (low risk) to e (high risk).
Path S / F / PPLr
S1 F1 P1a
S1 F1 P2b
S1 F2 P1b
S1 F2 P2c
S2 F1 P1c
S2 F1 P2d
S2 F2 P1d
S2 F2 P2e

SICK shows a typical case in its performance level blog where slight injury, frequent exposure and scarce avoidance lead to PLr c. Pilz notes that a low probability of the hazardous event occurring can reduce PLr by one level.

Quick Tip

Write down why you chose S, F and P for every hazard, because auditors ask for this reasoning more often than for the final ISO 13849 performance level.

ISO 13849 Performance Level PFHd Table

Every ISO 13849 performance level maps to a band of PFHd values in Table 2 of Part 1. The table below also lists the IEC 62061 SIL whose PFH limit lines up with each band, using the SIL limits quoted by Pilz.

PLPFHd per hourMatching SIL (IEC 62061)
a≥ 10minus 5 to < 10minus 4no SIL
b≥ 3 × 10minus 6 to < 10minus 5SIL 1
c≥ 10minus 6 to < 3 × 10minus 6SIL 1
d≥ 10minus 7 to < 10minus 6SIL 2
e≥ 10minus 8 to < 10minus 7SIL 3

What Are the Categories in ISO 13849?

A Category describes the structure of the safety circuit and how it behaves when a fault appears. It is the architecture half of the rating, while MTTFd, DCavg and CCF are the reliability half.

Category B

Single channel with basic safety principles and MTTFd low to medium.

Best for: Low risk functions
Max PL b
Category 1

Single channel with well tried components and MTTFd high.

Best for: Simple guard switches
Max PL c
Category 2

Single channel plus periodic testing, DCavg low to medium.

Best for: Light curtains Type 2
Max PL d
Category 3

Two channels, so a single fault does not lose the function.

Best for: Guard doors, E stops
Max PL e
Category 4

Two channels with MTTFd high and DCavg of 99 % or more.

Best for: Presses, robot cells
PL e

Category 3 and 4 circuits are usually built around a safety relay that monitors both channels and checks the feedback of two contactors. The idea of two channels is close to the 1oo2 logic covered in our note on voting architectures.

MTTFd, DCavg and CCF Bands

Once the Category is fixed, three numbers decide your final ISO 13849 performance level. Keyence publishes these bands in its safety knowledge pages.

ParameterBandValue
MTTFd per channelLow3 years ≤ MTTFd < 10 years
MTTFd per channelMedium10 years ≤ MTTFd < 30 years
MTTFd per channelHigh30 years ≤ MTTFd ≤ 100 years
DCavgNoneDC < 60 %
DCavgLow60 % ≤ DC < 90 %
DCavgMedium90 % ≤ DC < 99 %
DCavgHighDC ≥ 99 %
CCFPass65 points or more out of 100

MTTFd is the mean time to dangerous failure of one channel, much like the figure you get from an MTBF calculation but counting only dangerous failures. Festo notes that values above 100 years per channel are capped at 100 years, while Pilz points out that Category 4 allows up to 2,500 years.

DC, the diagnostic coverage, is the share of dangerous failures that your diagnostics detect. Engineers usually estimate it with a short failure mode and effects analysis of each sensor and output, and it plays a similar role to the safe failure fraction in IEC 61508 work.

CCF, the common cause failure score, checks that one event such as a voltage spike cannot knock out both channels together. Festo lists the measure groups as separation 15, diversity 20, design and application 20, assessment 5, competence and training 5 and environment 35 points.

Do You Know?

Diversity alone is worth 20 CCF points, so using one mechanical switch and one non contact coded sensor on the same door is a cheap way to strengthen a Category 3 design.

How to Calculate MTTFd From B10d?

Mechanical and electromechanical parts wear with operations rather than time, so makers quote B10d, the number of cycles until 10 % of samples fail dangerously. APEM and Festo both give the same conversion formula from the standard.

nop = dop × hop × 3600 ÷ tcycle
MTTFd = B10d ÷ (0.1 × nop)
dop = operating days per year
hop = operating hours per day
tcycle = seconds between operations

Festo adds that if a maker gives only B10, you may assume B10d = 2 × B10, meaning every second failure is treated as dangerous.

MTTFd From B10d Calculator
Result
nop = 23040 operations per year | MTTFd = 868.1 years | Band: High, use 100 years per channel
Quick Tip

The standard also limits the useful life of a worn part to T10d, which is B10d divided by nop. Plan replacement of contactors and switches before that point, just like you plan a proof test.

Advertisement

Solved Example: Guard Door Interlock

Take a packing machine in Pune where an operator opens a hinged guard every 10 minutes to clear jams. The risk assessment says S2 (crushing of fingers), F2 (frequent access) and P1 (the motor slows before contact), so the ISO 13849 performance level needed is PLr d.

SensorsOne positive opening switch and one coded non contact sensor.
LogicDual channel safety relay with cross monitoring.
OutputsTwo contactors in series with mirror contact feedback.
ResultCategory 3, DCavg medium assumed.
dop = 240 days, hop = 16 h, tcycle = 600 s
nop = 240 × 16 × 3600 ÷ 600 = 23,040 per year
Switch B10d = 2,000,000 cycles
MTTFd = 2,000,000 ÷ (0.1 × 23,040)
MTTFd = 868.1 years, use 100 years

With Category 3, MTTFd high per channel, DCavg medium and CCF of 65 points or more, the simplified bar chart of Annex K reaches PL e. Since the achieved PL e is better than PLr d, this guard door design passes, provided the contactors are checked the same way.

Repeat the check for the contactors using their own B10d at rated load, because the contactor often sets the lowest MTTFd. Our guide on failures in industrial automation shows why the output side fails first.

SISTEMA Tool for PL Calculation

SISTEMA is a free Windows tool from IFA, the safety institute of the German Social Accident Insurance, that models your blocks and channels and calculates the achieved PL. The DGUV page states that version 3.x follows ISO 13849 Part 1:2023 and that commercial use is allowed.

PDF
Safety@Festo: Evaluating Safety Measures to EN ISO 13849 1, EN 62061 and EN 61511
Festo guide with risk graph, categories, CCF points and B10d method

What Is the Difference Between PL and SIL?

PL comes from ISO 13849 and SIL for machinery comes from IEC 62061, while process plants use SIL under IEC 61511 for their safety instrumented functions. The table compares the three so you can pick the right standard.

PointISO 13849IEC 62061IEC 61511
SectorMachineryMachineryProcess industry
RatingPL a to eSIL 1 to 3SIL 1 to 4
Main metricPFHdPFHPFDavg or PFH
TechnologyAny (electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic)Electrical and programmableInstrumented systems

For process loops in low demand mode you calculate PFDavg instead of PFHd, which you can try with our PFDavg calculator. The broader picture of how these fit together is in process safety vs functional safety.

Strengths of the PL Method
  • Covers pneumatic and hydraulic parts, not only electronics
  • Free SISTEMA tool and wide maker libraries
  • Clear link between risk graph and design target
Limitations
  • Simplified method caps the result at PL e
  • Complex programmable logic often needs IEC 62061 or IEC 61508 detail
  • MTTFd figures depend heavily on assumed nop
Myth: A Category 4 circuit is always PL e.
Fact: Category sets structure only, and PL e also needs MTTFd high, DCavg high and CCF of 65 points or more.
Myth: Using a PL e safety relay makes the whole function PL e.
Fact: The weakest of sensor, logic and output limits the result, so a single cheap switch can pull it down.

Field Tips and Troubleshooting

SymptomLikely causeFix
Achieved PL one step below PLrLow MTTFd of contactor at high nopUse higher B10d contactor or reduce switching
Relay will not reset after door closesContactor feedback loop open or welded contactCheck mirror contacts and wiring
CCF score below 65Both channels in one cable, no diversitySeparate routing, mix sensor types

Never treat a bypass as a quick fix, because a defeated interlock drops the real PL to zero. Our notes on force vs override and on lockout tagout explain how maintenance access should be handled instead.

  • Risk assessment done and PLr recorded for every safety function
  • Category chosen and block diagram drawn for each channel
  • MTTFd per channel calculated from B10d with a realistic nop
  • CCF checklist scored at 65 points or more
  • SISTEMA report and validation per Part 2 filed with the machine

ISO 13849 Performance Level FAQ

What is the highest ISO 13849 performance level?

PL e is the highest ISO 13849 performance level, with PFHd from 10 to the power minus 8 up to below 10 to the power minus 7 per hour. It is usually needed where serious injury, frequent exposure and poor avoidance all come together.

Reaching it normally needs a Category 3 or Category 4 circuit with high MTTFd. Diagnostic coverage and common cause measures must also be strong enough to support it.

How is PLr determined?

PLr is read from the risk graph using severity, frequency of exposure and possibility of avoidance. Each parameter has two choices, so eight paths lead to PLr a through e.

The choice is made during risk assessment before the circuit is designed. Writing down the reasons for each choice helps reviewers and later audits understand the target you set.

What is the difference between PL and SIL?

PL comes from ISO 13849 and applies to any technology on machinery, including pneumatics and hydraulics. SIL comes from IEC 62061 for machinery or IEC 61511 for process plants and focuses on electrical and programmable systems.

The PFH bands line up closely, so PL d roughly matches SIL 2 and PL e roughly matches SIL 3. The methods and lifecycle documents still differ, so follow the standard your customer names.

What does MTTFd mean in ISO 13849?

MTTFd is the mean time to dangerous failure of one channel, expressed in years. It is graded as low from 3 to 10 years, medium from 10 to 30 years and high from 30 to 100 years.

For electromechanical parts it is calculated from B10d and the yearly number of operations. Values above 100 years are normally capped at 100 years when you work out the achieved level.

Why is a CCF score of 65 needed?

A CCF score of 65 points shows that you have enough measures against one cause failing both channels together. It is required for Categories 2, 3 and 4 in the standard.

Points come from separation, diversity, design, assessment, competence and environmental measures with a total of 100 points available. Scoring below 65 means redundancy cannot be fully credited in your calculation.

Is SISTEMA software free?

Yes, SISTEMA is offered free of charge by IFA, the safety institute of the German Social Accident Insurance. Its licence allows commercial, teaching and private use of the tool.

The tool models your channels and blocks and then calculates the achieved PL automatically. Version 3.x is aligned with the 2023 edition of ISO 13849 Part 1, so use it for new projects.

What We Learn Today

  • The iso 13849 performance level runs from PL a to PL e and is defined by the PFHd band of the safety function per hour.
  • PLr comes from the risk graph using severity, frequency and avoidance, and the achieved PL must be equal to or better than it.
  • Achieved PL depends on Category, MTTFd from B10d and nop, DCavg and a common cause failure score of at least 65 points.
